fact.claim: When Systems Manager uses AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints), traffic between managed instances, Systems Manager and Amazon EC2 stays on the Amazon network, the managed instances don't have access to the Internet, and you don't need an internet gateway, a NAT device or a virtual private gateway.
fact.question: Can interface VPC endpoints replace a NAT gateway for Systems Manager (Session Manager) on an instance in a private subnet?

values.display: don't need an internet gateway, a NAT device
values.spoken: no internet gateway and no NAT gateway needed

values.display: managed instances don't have access to the Internet
values.spoken: the instances have no internet access

qualifiers.scope: Systems Manager managed instances that use interface VPC endpoints
qualifiers.condition: interface VPC endpoints for Systems Manager are configured

evidence.quote: AWS PrivateLink restricts all network traffic between your managed instances, Systems Manager, and Amazon EC2 to the Amazon network. This means that your managed instances don't have access to the Internet. If you use AWS PrivateLink, you don't need an internet gateway, a NAT device, or a virtual private gateway.
evidence.title: Improve the security of EC2 instances by using VPC endpoints for Systems Manager

fact.note: fr-0061 (Session Manager network path for an instance in a private subnet). Page title: Improve the security of EC2 instances by using VPC endpoints for Systems Manager.

votes.reason: The quote supports the Amazon network restriction, no internet access and no internet gateway, NAT device or virtual private gateway, but it says AWS PrivateLink; the claim's scope 'interface VPC endpoints' stands only in the context sentence before the quote.
